claims.text: Recording, exporting and storing spans costs CPU, network and storage that grow with the number of requests traced; sampling keeps only some traces to cut that cost.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry docs 'Sampling' (why sample: cost of telemetry volume); opentelemetry-dotnet docs 'Customizing the SDK — Sampler'

claims.text: Head sampling: the sampling decision for a trace is made when its first (root) span starts, before the work has run, without seeing the rest of the trace.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry docs 'Sampling' (Head sampling); OpenTelemetry specification 'Trace SDK — Sampling'

claims.text: The sampled flag is the lowest bit of the trace flags, the last field of traceparent: ...-01 means the caller sampled (recorded) the trace, ...-00 that it did not; the sampling decision travels to later processes in this flag.
claims.source_hint: W3C Trace Context 'trace-flags' / 'Sampled flag'; .NET docs 'Distributed tracing concepts' (ActivityTraceFlags.Recorded)

claims.text: OpenTelemetry .NET ParentBasedSampler uses the sampling decision of the parent span when one exists; with no parent it delegates to the root sampler passed to its constructor.
OpenTelemetry .NET TraceIdRatioBasedSampler keeps a new (root) trace with a fixed probability given to its constructor.

A span the SDK does not sample is neither recorded nor exported: in trace-sampling.sh the trace marked 00 has no spans in Tempo. Services that follow the flag they receive keep or drop the same trace.
claims.source_hint: opentelemetry-dotnet docs 'Customizing the SDK — Sampler' (Drop: not recorded/exported); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 outputs/stage-3/scripts/backend/trace-sampling.txt

claims.text: Head sampling cannot keep a trace because of its outcome (an error, a slow request); keeping traces by outcome needs a component that waits for the complete trace before deciding. Đơn Hàng has no such component at stage-3.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry docs 'Sampling' (Head sampling downsides; Tail sampling); examples/don-hang @ stage-3 deploy/monitoring/alloy/config.alloy (no sampling stage)

claims.text: With a 0.1 ratio, about 9 in 10 traces that start in the api are dropped on average, including those of rare errors.
DonHang.Api/Program.cs (lines 101-116) reads Telemetry:SampleRatio with GetValue, fallback 0.1, and calls SetSampler(new ParentBasedSampler(new TraceIdRatioBasedSampler(sampleRatio))).
IConfiguration GetValue<T>(key, defaultValue) returns defaultValue when the key is absent; the environment variable Telemetry__SampleRatio maps to the key Telemetry:SampleRatio.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs 'Configuration' (GetValue; environment variables, double underscore as separator)

Sampling only decides whether spans are recorded and exported; it does not change how the request is handled or its response.

prometheus-net is the api's metrics library: UseHttpMetrics keeps http_requests_received_total, served at /metrics for Prometheus; it counts every request (except /metrics) independently of tracing, so sampling does not change it.

claims.text: Try it: with the monitoring profile up, scripts/backend/trace-sampling.sh prints 1 span for the 01 trace, 0 for the 00 trace, and 2 for the counter.

Each service's sampler and ratio are its own configuration, so nothing makes separate decisions match; a parent-based sampler in every service follows the flag it receives, so every service makes the same decision.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry .NET docs 'Sampling' (ParentBased: consistent sampling decisions across services in the same trace)
